question: Can a fully open post-training recipe (data, evaluation, SFT, DPO and a new RL stage) on Llama 3.1 base models match or beat the instruct versions of open models and some closed models?
hypothesis: Careful data curation and decontamination, on-policy preference data, and an RL stage with verifiable rewards will improve targeted skills (math, precise instruction following) without hurting the others.
contributions: Extensive guidance and tooling for evaluation, decontamination, and recipe design
Scaling preference data with on-policy generations
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), an RL-based method that only gets a reward if the model's completions are verified to be correct
Advanced infrastructure, details, and code to facilitate the successful implementation of large models

method.summary: A four-stage post-training pipeline on Llama 3.1 8B/70B/405B base models: prompt curation and decontamination, SFT on about 939k prompts, length-normalized DPO on a synthetic on-policy plus off-policy preference mix (LLM-judge labels from GPT-4o), then PPO with a binary verifiable reward (RLVR) on about 30k GSM8K/MATH/IFEval-style prompts. Evaluated on a development suite and a separate unseen suite (Tülu 3 Eval / OLMES).
method.task: multi-stage LLM post-training: SFT, preference optimisation (DPO), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (PPO)

datasets.name: Tülu 3 prompt pool (Table 7)
datasets.size: 23,327,961 prompts in pool; 939,344 used in SFT; 425,145 in DPO prompt pool (not all in both 8B and 70B mixes)
datasets.source: public datasets (WildChat GPT-4 subset, OpenAssistant, No Robots, FLAN v2, UltraFeedback, SciRIFF, TableGPT, OpenMathInstruct 2, NuminaMath-TIR, Evol CodeAlpaca, Aya, CoCoNot, WildJailbreak, WildGuardMix) plus new persona-driven synthetic sets (Persona MATH/GSM/Algebra/Python/IF, IF-augmented, hardcoded)
datasets.preprocessing: filtered for specific keywords (e.g. OpenAI) and empty messages; decontaminated with 8-gram matching against dev and unseen evals; ShareGPT and HelpSteer2 excluded for provenance

datasets.name: Tülu 3 SFT mix
datasets.source: responses kept from human/frontier models, otherwise regenerated with GPT-4o (claude-3-5-sonnet for Persona code)
datasets.preprocessing: empty responses and responses naming models/developers removed; personas: about 250K from Persona Hub

datasets.name: Tülu 3 preference mix
datasets.size: 354,192 total listed in Table 15; 271,409 (8B mix) and 334,302 (70B mix)
datasets.source: 4 responses per prompt from a 22-model pool (Table 38 lists external models) plus Tülu 3 SFT on-policy; GPT-4o-2024-08-06 rates 1-5 on helpfulness, instruction-following, honesty, truthfulness; chosen = highest mean, rejected = random from below-mean
datasets.preprocessing: binarised following Argilla's mean-rating method; components: SFT reused on-policy 19,444, SFT reused off-policy 96,911, IF-augmented 65,530, WildChat IF 10,792, WildChat reused 17,207, WildChat unused 82,783 (70B only), UltraFeedback cleaned 41,635, Persona IF 19,890 (70B only)

datasets.name: RLVR prompts (Table 22)
datasets.size: 29,946 prompts: GSM8K train 7,473; MATH train 7,500; IF verifiable 14,973
datasets.source: GSM8K, MATH, and IFEval-style constraints appended to Tülu 2 SFT mix prompts
datasets.preprocessing: GSM8K gets the standard 8-shot prompt, MATH the 3-shot CoT prompt; verification by exact match against extracted answer, or per-constraint verifier functions

datasets.name: Tülu 3 Eval development suite
datasets.split: MMLU, PopQA, TruthfulQA, BBH, DROP, MATH, GSM8K, HumanEval, HumanEval+, IFEval, AlpacaEval 2, Tülu 3 Safety (6 benchmarks)

datasets.name: Tülu 3 Eval unseen suite
datasets.split: MMLU-Pro, GPQA, AGIEval English, DeepMind Mathematics, BigCodeBench-Hard (148 of 1140 instances), IFEval-OOD (52 constraints), HREF
datasets.source: not examined during model development; no unseen safety eval

models.name: Tülu 3 8B / 70B / 405B (SFT, DPO, RLVR checkpoints)
models.init_from: Llama 3.1 base, then SFT -> DPO -> RLVR

models.name: Tülu 3 8B RM
models.architecture: Tülu 3 SFT with linear reward head initialised N(0, 1/sqrt(d_model+1)); reward from EOS-token logit

other.use: initialises the PPO value model for RLVR; trained on the Tülu 3 8B preference mixture; 9 hours on 8 H100

models.name: Llama 3.1 Instruct, Qwen 2.5 Instruct, Gemma 2 Instruct, Ministral, Hermes 3, Nemotron Llama 3.1 70B, Magpie, DeepSeek V3, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-3.5 Turbo, Claude 3.5 Haiku

training.objective: SFT: sum-reduced token loss. DPO: length-normalized DPO (Eq. 6) with beta = 5. RLVR: PPO on max E[v(x,y) - beta*KL(pi||pi_ref)] with v = alpha if correct else 0, alpha = 10.
training.warmup: SFT ratio 0.03; DPO ratio 0.1; RLVR 8B omega = 0.0 in final, 70B 0.07 (Table 21 caption) or 0.1 (Sec 6.4 text); 405B RLVR 0.0
training.steps: 405B RLVR: 75 steps; 8B/70B RLVR checkpoints chosen every 100 steps (40 for 70B) by dev eval
training.epochs: SFT 2; DPO 1; RM 1; RLVR ablations about 100,000/7,473 = 13 epochs of prompts
training.seq_len: SFT max 4,096 tokens (405B too); DPO max 2,048; RM 2,048; PPO max token length 2,048, response length 1,024 (RM-PPO) or 2,048 (1,024 for GSM8K only) for RLVR
training.dropout: disabled (0) during RM and RL training
training.regularisation: KL penalty: DPO beta = 5; RLVR final 8B beta = 0.05, 70B beta = 0.07 (Table 21 caption) or 0.7 (Sec 6.4 text); 405B beta = 0.05. PPO: gamma 1.0, GAE lambda 0.95, clip 0.2, value coeff 0.1, grad norm 1.0, non-EOS penalty -10, advantage whitening, generation temperature 1.0
training.hardware: SFT 4-16 nodes of 8xH100; 8B SFT 32 GPUs; 70B SFT 64 GPUs; 8B DPO 8 H100; 70B DPO 64 H100; 8B RM 8 H100; 8B RLVR 8 GPUs; 70B RLVR 48 GPUs; 405B RLVR 256 GPUs (32 nodes, 16 GPUs vLLM inference, 240 training)
training.wall_clock: 8B SFT 6 hours; 70B SFT 50 hours; 8B DPO 10 hours; 70B DPO 19 hours; 8B RM 9 hours; 8B RLVR 65 hours; 70B RLVR 60 hours; 405B RLVR 46 hours (earlier-than-final checkpoint taken for all RL runs). PPO-vs-DPO ablation: PPO about 28 h on two nodes, DPO about 4 h on one node.
training.seeds: SFT seeds 42/123/456/789/1011 (8B) and 42/123/456 (70B) compared; best single run used. RL/DPO seeds not stated.

other.value_model_init: from the general RM (Tülu 3 8B RM) for all RLVR runs; best in ablation
other.async_RL: policy trained on second-latest inference data; inference on vLLM with dedicated GPUs; ZeRO stage 3; Ray
other.405B_RLVR: only MATH train prompts (GSM8K saturated, IFEval did not help); 8B value model; weight sync via NCCL; inference about 550 s, weight transfer about 25 s, training about 1,500 s per iteration; 300,000 total episodes in Table 35
other.dpo_infra: cache reference log-probs; separate forward passes for chosen and rejected
other.model_soups: tried with mergekit linear averaging; best soup not better than best single run
other.final_checkpoint_selection: 8B final: best overall on MATH and IFEval among checkpoints; ablations use anchored DPO model

inference.decoding: greedy for most dev evals; HumanEval/HumanEval+ sampled at temperature 0.8 with pass@10; AlpacaEval 2 greedy up to 8,192 tokens; generative eval output length 4096
inference.temperature: 1.0 during PPO rollouts; 0.8 for HumanEval pass@10; greedy otherwise
inference.samples: pass@10 for HumanEval, HumanEval+, BigCodeBench; one greedy sample otherwise; one RM trained once
inference.prompting: see Table 24: MMLU 0-shot CoT ('summarize your reasoning'), PopQA 15-shot, TruthfulQA 6-shot MC2, BBH 3-shot CoT, DROP 3-shot, GSM8K 8-shot CoT, MATH 4-shot CoT flex, multiturn ICL where marked; unseen suite 0-shot CoT

eval.protocol: Single run per final model; closed-model scores partly taken from model cards (⊤) or imputed with MICE (♢) in Table 2; unseen suite not looked at during development; decontamination with 8-gram match, >50% token overlap per instance, dataset dropped if >2% of an eval overlaps. No significance tests or variance for DPO/RLVR.

prompts.text: Your role is to evaluate text quality based on given criteria. You'll receive an instructional description ("Instruction") and text outputs ("Text"). Understand and interpret instructions to evaluate effectively. Provide annotations for each text with a rating and rationale. The texts given are independent, and should be evaluated separately.
The following are multiple choice questions about {MMLU subject}. Summarize your reasoning concisely, then conclude with 'Therefore, the answer is: X' where X is one of A, B, C, or D.

limits: Preference-tuning algorithm ablations (Table 18) use an early SFT checkpoint and UltraFeedback only, with batch size 32, one run each, no variance reported.
PPO vs DPO comparison is described by the authors as a non-tuned setup: the reward model was trained once and not tuned, so the PPO result could rise with more tuning or compute.

RLVR covers only math (GSM8K, MATH) and verifiable instruction following; more complex verifiers left to future work; development and RLVR targets overlap with eval benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH, IFEval), and IFEval-OOD shows overfitting to IFEval constraints.
All final 8B/70B/405B RL checkpoints are earlier than the final saved step; 405B RLVR stopped at 75 steps because of compute and MATH had not saturated.
No long-context, multi-turn, multilingual, tool-use or agent training (Sec 8.3); English focus; mean 2.4 turns.
Cannot rule out that closed models trained on the eval suite; some closed-model numbers were imputed (MICE) or taken from model cards.
Single run per configuration for DPO and RLVR; seed variation shown only for SFT (Table 14), where it was noticeable.
Internal inconsistency: 70B RLVR KL coefficient and warmup are 0.07/0.07 in the Table 21 caption but 0.7/0.1 in Sec 6.4 text.
Dev-suite comparisons are dated to Nov 2024 open and closed models.

terms.definition: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards: the RLHF objective with the reward model replaced by a verification function v(x,y) that returns alpha if the answer is verifiably correct and 0 otherwise, optimised with PPO after preference tuning.
DPO with the log-probability ratios divided by response length, aiding in mitigating length bias.
preference pairs where one response is sampled from the SFT model that will be tuned, and the other from off-policy models.
development set used to guide training decisions; unseen set only for final models and for checking overfitting to dev evals.
